newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Ramos apologises for Mitterrand gaffe.
newsitem.headline: Ramos apologises for Mitterrand gaffe.

text.p: President Fidel Ramos publicly apologised on Sunday for erroneously saying that former French first lady Danielle Mitterrand was dead.
"Okay, I made a mistake and I apologise to everybody and I will apologise personally by way of a letter to Madame Mitterrand," he told reporters on southern Camiguin island.
"I'm sorry about it. We'll try to make amends to Madame Mitterrand and the people of France and the government of France."
In a gaffe that titillated Manila's rambunctious press, Ramos referred on Saturday to the very much alive widow of late French president Francois Mitterrand as already dead.
"Why should we (ban) the French first lady, Danielle Mitterrand, who died already," he said in southern Davao city.
"I should know. I wrote a letter of condolences to President Mitterrand," he said, apparently referring to condolences he sent Mrs Mitterrand when her husband died of cancer in January.

Ramos was denying Manila press reports that the government had a list of 100 foreigners barred from the country during next month's Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) forum summit. Newspapers had said Mrs Mitterrand was on the list.

Ramos earlier banned Nobel peace laureate and East Timorese resistance leader Jose Ramos-Horta from entering the country to speak on the East Timor issue at a conference of non-governmental organisations coinciding with APEC meetings.
Indonesian President Suharto, whose country annexed the former Portuguese colony in 1976 in a move never recognised by the United Nations, is expected to attend the APEC summit.
"Oops! Ramos "kills' wrong Mitterrand," a headline in the Philippine Daily Inquirer newspaper said on Sunday.
The Malaya (Free) daily said in its headline: "Danielle Mitterrand is alive and well, thank you."
